Musical artist

**Jon Brion** (born December 11, 1963) is an American singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and composer. He performed with the Excerpts, the Bats, ['Til Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/'Til_Tuesday "'Til Tuesday"), and [the Grays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grays_(band) "The Grays (band)") before becoming an established producer and film score composer.

Brion has produced music for artists and bands including [Of Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Of_Montreal "Of Montreal"), [Aimee Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aimee_Mann "Aimee Mann"), [Love Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Jones_(band) "Love Jones (band)"), [Eels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eels_(band) "Eels (band)"), [Fiona Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiona_Apple "Fiona Apple"), [Robyn Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robyn_Hitchcock "Robyn Hitchcock"), [Rhett Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhett_Miller "Rhett Miller"), [The Crystal Method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crystal_Method "The Crystal Method"), [Frank Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean"), [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"), [Sky Ferreira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Ferreira "Sky Ferreira") and [Mac Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Miller "Mac Miller").

Brion's film scores include _[Hard Eight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard\_Eight\_(film) "Hard Eight (film)")_ (1996), _[Magnolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnolia\_(film) "Magnolia (film)")_ (1999), _[Punch-Drunk Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punch-Drunk\_Love "Punch-Drunk Love")_ (2002), _[Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal\_Sunshine\_of\_the\_Spotless\_Mind "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind"),_ and _[I Heart Huckabees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Heart\_Huckabees "I Heart Huckabees")_ (both 2004), _[Synecdoche, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synecdoche,\_New\_York "Synecdoche, New York")_ (2008), _[ParaNorman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ParaNorman "ParaNorman")_ (2012), _[Lady Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady\_Bird\_(film) "Lady Bird (film)")_ (2017), and _[Christopher Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher\_Robin\_(film) "Christopher Robin (film)")_ (2018). He released his debut solo album, _[Meaningless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meaningless\_(album) "Meaningless (album)")_, in 2001.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Brion was born in [Glen Ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Ridge,_New_Jersey "Glen Ridge, New Jersey"), [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), on December 11, 1963. He comes from a musical family; his mother, LaRue, was a singer and administrative assistant, and his father, [Keith Brion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Brion "Keith Brion"), was a band director at [Yale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale "Yale").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-1) His brother and sister became a composer/arranger and a violinist, respectively. Brion grew up in Connecticut, where he dropped out of [Hamden High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamden_High_School "Hamden High School") at the age of 17, opting instead to play music professionally. From 1980 to 1985 Jon was part of the band The Excerpts, along with Stephen Harris, Dean Falcone, Jim Balga, Bobby Butcher & Spike Priggen.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-2)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### The Bats

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: The Bats")]

In the early 1980s, Brion and musician/producer Bill Murphy began a writing collaboration in [New Haven, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven,_Connecticut "New Haven, Connecticut"). They eventually enlisted bassist Don "Riff" Fertman and together formed the Bats (not to be confused with the [New Zealand group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bats_(New_Zealand_band) "The Bats (New Zealand band)") or [South African group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bats_(South_African_band) "The Bats (South African band)") of the same name). The Bats released a single, "Popgun", and one album, _[How Pop Can You Get?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How\_Pop\_Can\_You\_Get%3F "How Pop Can You Get?")_, on Gustav Records in 1982. The recordings had much critical acclaim, but little commercial success, and the trio eventually disbanded.

### Session work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Session work")]

In 1987, Brion moved to [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), where he played solo gigs, formed the short-lived band World's Fair and became a member of the last touring version of [Aimee Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aimee_Mann "Aimee Mann")'s [new wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_wave_music "New wave music") band ['Til Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/'Til_Tuesday "'Til Tuesday"). He contributed guitar work to [Jellyfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jellyfish_(band) "Jellyfish (band)")'s 1993 album [_Spilt Milk_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spilt_Milk_(Jellyfish_album) "Spilt Milk (Jellyfish album)"), and in 1994, joined Dan McCarroll, Buddy Judge and ex-Jellyfish guitarist [Jason Falkner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Falkner "Jason Falkner") in the short-lived pop band [the Grays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Grays_(band) "The Grays (band)"). He also played guitar on [the Wallflowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wallflowers "The Wallflowers")' hit song "[One Headlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Headlight "One Headlight")", using a screwdriver that was sitting atop a nearby amp as a slide.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-3) Brion played numerous instruments on [Sam Phillips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Phillips_(singer) "Sam Phillips (singer)")' 1996 release _[Omnipop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omnipop\_(It's\_Only\_A\_Fleshwound\_Lambchop) "Omnipop (It's Only A Fleshwound Lambchop)")_. Brion is featured as keyboardist and drummer on [Marianne Faithfull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marianne_Faithfull "Marianne Faithfull")'s 2003 album, _[Kissin Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kissin\_Time "Kissin Time")_, and co-wrote a song, "City of Quartz", for her next work, 2005's _[Before the Poison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before\_the\_Poison "Before the Poison")_. In 2009, Brion contributed mutli-instrumentation to the Nonesuch [[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-4) debut, [Christina Courtin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Courtin "Christina Courtin").

### Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production")]

After being recognized as an accomplished session player, Brion branched out into production on then-girlfriend Mann's 1993 solo debut, _[Whatever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatever\_(Aimee\_Mann\_album) "Whatever (Aimee Mann album)")_, and its follow-up, _[I'm With Stupid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_with\_Stupid\_(album) "I'm with Stupid (album)")_. He has also produced albums by [Fiona Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiona_Apple "Fiona Apple"), [Rufus Wainwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_Wainwright "Rufus Wainwright"), [Eleni Mandell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleni_Mandell "Eleni Mandell"), [Rhett Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhett_Miller "Rhett Miller"), [Robyn Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robyn_Hitchcock "Robyn Hitchcock"), [Brad Mehldau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Mehldau "Brad Mehldau") and [Evan Dando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Dando "Evan Dando"), and co-produced [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West")'s _[Late Registration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Registration "Late Registration")_ in 2005.

In the fall of 2002, Brion began producing the album _[Extraordinary Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraordinary\_Machine "Extraordinary Machine")_ with Fiona Apple, but she later brought in producers [Mike Elizondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Elizondo "Mike Elizondo") and [Brian Kehew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Kehew "Brian Kehew") (a friend of Brion's) to complete the album. Brion's versions leaked onto the Internet, where the album gained a cult following long before its official release.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-5)

Brion worked and performed on some of the tracks for [Sean Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Lennon "Sean Lennon")'s 2006 album _[Friendly Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friendly\_Fire\_(Sean\_Lennon\_album) "Friendly Fire (Sean Lennon album)")_. Lennon said that working with him was "how I would imagine it's like to work with [Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_(musician) "Prince (musician)"). It's like having a weird alien prodigy in your room."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-6)

Brion has produced recordings by British pop performer [Dido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dido_(singer) "Dido (singer)"), [Spoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spoon_(band) "Spoon (band)"), and [Keane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keane_(band) "Keane (band)"), as well as 2010's _[False Priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False\_Priest "False Priest")_ by [Of Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Of_Montreal "Of Montreal"). Brion also produced [Best Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Coast "Best Coast")'s second album which was released in early 2012.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-7) Brion worked on rapper [Mac Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Miller "Mac Miller")'s album _[Swimming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming\_(Mac\_Miller\_album) "Swimming (Mac Miller album)")_ (2018), and completed production on Miller's posthumous album _[Circles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circles\_(Mac\_Miller\_album) "Circles (Mac Miller album)")_ (2020).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-Circles_announcement-8)

According to _[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum"),_ Brion's work on Aimee Mann's first solo albums "lay the groundwork for a sound that became synonymous with a strain of notable alternative acts at the turn of the century".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-stereogum-9)

### _Meaningless_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Meaningless")]

Brion was signed to the [Lava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava_Records "Lava Records")/[Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records") label in 1997, but was released from his contract after turning in his solo debut album _[Meaningless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meaningless\_(album) "Meaningless (album)")_; the album was released independently in 2001. In 2022, the album was remastered and re-released through Jealous Butcher Records, with Brion's approval.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-10)

Although, rumors persist about Brion working on a second solo full-length album[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_], as of 2023, an album has not been forthcoming. In 2004, Aimee Mann stated "Jon has at least 10 albums' worth of material," and "I think he has a hard time saying anything is finished whether he's producing or doing his own songs. Jon's a perfectionist."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-11)

### Film scores

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Film scores")]

Brion is an accomplished film composer, having started scoring by frequently working with director [Paul Thomas Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Thomas_Anderson "Paul Thomas Anderson"), with whom he collaborated on the director’s first three movies. In addition to scoring many of his films, Brion contributed music to _[Boogie Nights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie\_Nights "Boogie Nights")_ and had a cameo in the film as a moustached guitar player.

Particularly in his film soundtracks, Brion is noted for his use of early analog sampling instruments, particularly the [Chamberlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamberlin "Chamberlin") and [Optigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optigan "Optigan"), to create near-realistic emulations of certain instruments.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-12)

He has earned [Best Score Soundtrack Album Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Score_Soundtrack_Album_for_a_Motion_Picture,_Television_or_Other_Visual_Media "Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack Album for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media") nominations for his work on 1999's _[Magnolia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnolia\_(movie) "Magnolia (movie)")_ and 2004's _[Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal\_Sunshine\_of\_the\_Spotless\_Mind "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind")_.

Brion was hired at the last minute to write the incidental music for _[The Break-Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Break-Up "The Break-Up")_. He has also scored and provided original music for _[I Heart Huckabees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Heart\_Huckabees "I Heart Huckabees")_, _[Punch-Drunk Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punch-Drunk\_Love "Punch-Drunk Love")_, _[Step Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Brothers\_(film) "Step Brothers (film)")_ (with [Chris Thile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Thile "Chris Thile")), _[ParaNorman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ParaNorman "ParaNorman")_, _[The Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Future\_(film) "The Future (film)")_, _[Synecdoche, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synecdoche,\_New\_York "Synecdoche, New York"),_[Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig")'s _[Lady Bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady\_Bird\_(film) "Lady Bird (film)")_ and Disney's _[Christopher Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher\_Robin\_(film) "Christopher Robin (film)")_ (with [Geoff Zanelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Zanelli "Geoff Zanelli")). He also did live composition for a musical commentary on the _Step Brothers_ DVD.

He also composed the score to the Disney/[Pixar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixar "Pixar") short film, _The Blue Umbrella_, working alongside Sarah Jaffe.

Two previously unreleased tracks of Brion's were used in the score of Paul Thomas Anderson's 2025 film _[One Battle After Another](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_Battle\_After\_Another "One Battle After Another")._

## Touring and live performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jon_Brion&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Touring and live performances")]

Brion is renowned for his regular Friday-night gigs at the Los Angeles club [Largo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largo_(nightclub) "Largo (nightclub)"), which feature covers and original songs, a variety of instruments and occasional guest musicians and comedians. He works without a set list, instead using audience suggestions as a jumping-off point. He uses a "jigsaw puzzle" approach to performing songs, and uses looping systems to record himself starting often with drums, then adding piano, bass, guitar, and vocals. Over the years, shows have featured spontaneous appearances with [Jackson Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Browne "Jackson Browne"), [Gillian Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gillian_Welch "Gillian Welch"), [Fiona Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiona_Apple "Fiona Apple"), [Rickie Lee Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickie_Lee_Jones "Rickie Lee Jones") with upright bassist Stephen Patt (ex-[The Chambers Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chambers_Brothers "The Chambers Brothers")), [Aimee Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aimee_Mann "Aimee Mann"), [Elliott Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Smith "Elliott Smith"), [Ben Folds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Folds "Ben Folds"), [Nels Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nels_Cline "Nels Cline"), percussionist [Matt Chamberlain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Chamberlain "Matt Chamberlain"), [Tori Amos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tori_Amos "Tori Amos"), bassist [Sebastian Steinberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Steinberg "Sebastian Steinberg") (ex-[Soul Coughing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_Coughing "Soul Coughing")), and fiddler [Sara Watkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Watkins "Sara Watkins") ([Nickel Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickel_Creek "Nickel Creek")).

On March 24th, 2004, Brion performed an experimental live show with [John Frusciante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Frusciante "John Frusciante") ([Red Hot Chili Peppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hot_Chili_Peppers "Red Hot Chili Peppers")) and friends at The Knitting Factory in Los Angeles, playing a variety of keys and percussion. The show was labelled "Performance #9" and featured fellow artists [Josh Klinghoffer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Klinghoffer "Josh Klinghoffer") and [Carla Azar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carla_Azar "Carla Azar") on drums as well as [Flea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flea_(musician) "Flea (musician)") and [Eric Avery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Avery "Eric Avery") on bass. [John Frusciante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Frusciante "John Frusciante") played electric guitar, his Doepfer A-100 modular synthesiser and provided vocals.

In April 2006, recurring tendonitis in Brion's right hand forced him to cancel all of his upcoming Largo shows.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-13) As a temporary 'farewell', he played one show only using his left hand, even looping his songs as he normally does and playing the drums with one stick. He resumed playing at Largo on a regular weekly basis later that year, transitioning to a monthly show in 2016,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-14) until the COVID-19 Pandemic.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-15) In summer 2023, Brion stated to Largo at the Coronet that he intended to resume shows in the near future.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-16) Brion resumed shows at Largo in September 2023.[](https://www.instagram.com/reel/CxN28HMLDRV/?igshid=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==)

Recalling his approach to the Largo shows with _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ music editor Lou Carlozo, Brion said: "I taught my hands to follow whatever was coming into my head—and wherever my consciousness would go, I had to push my hands to follow. And at some level, you just had to abandon any concern about how you'd look. Performing without a set list: That was special."

In March 2016, Brion performed his score for _[Punch-Drunk Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punch-Drunk\_Love "Punch-Drunk Love")_ with [Wordless Music Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordless_Music_Orchestra?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wordless Music Orchestra (page does not exist)") in both Los Angeles and New York City, at the [Ace Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_Hotel "Ace Hotel") and the [Brooklyn Academy of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Academy_of_Music "Brooklyn Academy of Music"), respectively. [Norah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norah_Jones "Norah Jones") provided guest vocals in New York and [Joanna Newsom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_Newsom "Joanna Newsom") in Los Angeles.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-17)

In February 2018, Brion opened for [John Mulaney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mulaney "John Mulaney") as part of Mulaney's special, _Kid Gorgeous_. Brion performed during Mulaney's New York City leg of his tour, playing classic rock songs on Radio City's [Mighty Wurlitzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wurlitzer "Wurlitzer")[theatre organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatre_organ "Theatre organ").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Brion#cite_note-18)

Extraction uses the original question and current page, not the search query or
parent's hypothesis. Keep facts relevant to any part of the original question.
During navigation, a supplied local relation is a task, not evidence. Follow links
that establish or contradict it. Return when it is settled or has no useful route

question again inside every branch.

Preserve exact relevant names and rows with their headers, values, units, dates
and scope. Never replace relevant rows with ellipses, examples or instructions to
continue the list. If all rows cannot fit, prioritize rows useful to the question
and explicitly mark omissions. A partial, restricted or truncated list is not the
complete candidate set. Missing fields are unknown. Keep relevant discoveries even
if they answer a different part of the original question.

document/year. An index is useful when it offers a concrete route to the needed
record; generic menus or keyword collections alone do not justify expansion.
Link-menu rank is only a hint: check the destination's subject and scope. If content
repeats, try a detail page or another supported route. Links outside the menu and inferred
paths on an observed site are allowed. Child notes are returned automatically;
do not copy their facts into your own note. Retain useful unvisited links even
when expansion stops.

Photo: Zimbio[/caption] vocals Z...") overview

Elizabeth Anne “Z” Berg, born on June 28, 1986, is an accomplished American musician known for her dynamic contributions to indie rock. As a founding member, [guitar](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/guitar/ "[caption id=\"attachment_5802\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"200\"] Doug Derryberry on guitar[/caption] Played by: George Marinelli on: The Way It Is (album) Scenes from the Southside Night on the Town (album) Greatest Radio Hits David Mansfield on: The Way It Is (album) Night on the Town (album) Greatest Radio Hits Peter Harris on: Scenes from the Southside Greatest Radio...")ist, and lead vocalist of the band the Like, she began her musical journey at the age of 15. Berg is the daughter of [Tony Berg](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/tony-berg/ "Tony Berg is a music producer, guitarist, and songwriter known for his work with artists like Phoebe Bridgers, Andrew Bird, and Aimee Mann. Albums: Harbor Lights (album) - guitar chords on China Doll Indigo Park (album) Instruments: [caption id=\"attachment_4684\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"300\"] Tony Berg[/caption] guitar chords bass guitar banjo Tony's daughter Z Berg has also recorded with Bruce.  "), a former Geffen Records A&R executive and record producer.

#### Musical evolution

After the Like went on hiatus in 2011, Berg formed JJAMZ with James Valentine (Maroon 5), Jason Boesel (Bright Eyes/Rilo Kiley), Alex Greenwald (Phantom Planet), and Michael Runion. Their debut album, “Suicide Pact”, was released on July 10, 2012. Following Valentine’s departure, the band was rebranded as Phases, releasing “For Life” on September 18, 2015. Music critic Dan Cairns has described Berg’s voice as reminiscent of “Björk meets Harriet Wheeler.”

#### Solo projects

In 2018, [Z Berg](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/z-berg/ "Z Berg is a singer-songwriter known for her work as the frontwoman of the band The Like and her solo projects, blending pop and indie influences in her music. Albums: Levitate (album) - vocals on Invisible Flicted - vocals on Simple Prayer II Indigo Park (album) Instruments: [caption id=\"attachment_4687\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"201\"] Z Berg. Photo: Zimbio[/caption] vocals Z...") released several solo tracks, including “I Fall For the Same Face Every Time” and “Time Flies,” the latter of which she also directed the music video for. She continued to showcase her talent with the release of “All Out of Tears” later that year. In December 2018, she collaborated with Ryan Ross on the Christmas single “The Bad List.”

The following year, she embarked on “The Dead End Kids Club” tour alongside Ryan Ross, Dan Keyes, and Palm Springsteen. Berg released her debut solo album, “Get Z to a Nunnery”, in July 2020, followed by the original motion picture soundtrack for “Strange Darling” in 2024, further establishing her as a multifaceted artist in the music industry.

### [Z Berg](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/z-berg/ "Z Berg is a singer-songwriter known for her work as the frontwoman of the band The Like and her solo projects, blending pop and indie influences in her music. Albums: Levitate (album) - vocals on Invisible Flicted - vocals on Simple Prayer II Indigo Park (album) Instruments: [caption id=\"attachment_4687\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"201\"] Z Berg. Photo: Zimbio[/caption] vocals Z...") overview

Elizabeth Anne “Z” Berg, born on June 28, 1986, is an accomplished American musician known for her dynamic contributions to indie rock. As a founding member, [guitar](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/guitar/ "[caption id=\"attachment_5802\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"200\"] Doug Derryberry on guitar[/caption] Played by: George Marinelli on: The Way It Is (album) Scenes from the Southside Night on the Town (album) Greatest Radio Hits David Mansfield on: The Way It Is (album) Night on the Town (album) Greatest Radio Hits Peter Harris on: Scenes from the Southside Greatest Radio...")ist, and lead vocalist of the band the Like, she began her musical journey at the age of 15. Berg is the daughter of [Tony Berg](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/tony-berg/ "Tony Berg is a music producer, guitarist, and songwriter known for his work with artists like Phoebe Bridgers, Andrew Bird, and Aimee Mann. Albums: Harbor Lights (album) - guitar chords on China Doll Indigo Park (album) Instruments: [caption id=\"attachment_4684\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"300\"] Tony Berg[/caption] guitar chords bass guitar banjo Tony's daughter Z Berg has also recorded with Bruce.  "), a former Geffen Records A&R executive and record producer.

#### Musical evolution

After the Like went on hiatus in 2011, Berg formed JJAMZ with James Valentine (Maroon 5), Jason Boesel (Bright Eyes/Rilo Kiley), Alex Greenwald (Phantom Planet), and Michael Runion. Their debut album, “Suicide Pact”, was released on July 10, 2012. Following Valentine’s departure, the band was rebranded as Phases, releasing “For Life” on September 18, 2015. Music critic Dan Cairns has described Berg’s voice as reminiscent of “Björk meets Harriet Wheeler.”

#### Solo projects

In 2018, [Z Berg](https://bruuuce.com/wiki/z-berg/ "Z Berg is a singer-songwriter known for her work as the frontwoman of the band The Like and her solo projects, blending pop and indie influences in her music. Albums: Levitate (album) - vocals on Invisible Flicted - vocals on Simple Prayer II Indigo Park (album) Instruments: [caption id=\"attachment_4687\" align=\"alignright\" width=\"201\"] Z Berg. Photo: Zimbio[/caption] vocals Z...") released several solo tracks, including “I Fall For the Same Face Every Time” and “Time Flies,” the latter of which she also directed the music video for. She continued to showcase her talent with the release of “All Out of Tears” later that year. In December 2018, she collaborated with Ryan Ross on the Christmas single “The Bad List.”

The following year, she embarked on “The Dead End Kids Club” tour alongside Ryan Ross, Dan Keyes, and Palm Springsteen. Berg released her debut solo album, “Get Z to a Nunnery”, in July 2020, followed by the original motion picture soundtrack for “Strange Darling” in 2024, further establishing her as a multifaceted artist in the music industry.

They became a big hit with fans and made a place for themselves in the music world with a succession of big-selling albums. In the beginning of 2002, Justin spent time working on and writing songs for his debut solo album. During this time, he broke up with his longtime girlfriend, [Britney Spears](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005453/?ls). The release of the solo album, titled "Justified", came in November of 2002. Songs from his solo album include: "Like I Love You", "Cry Me A River" and "Rock Your Body".  
  
Timberlake has branched out into an acting career, having most recently starred in [The Social Network (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1285016/?ls), [Friends with Benefits (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1632708/?ls), and [Trouble with the Curve (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2083383/?ls).

Enrique Miguel Iglesias Preysler was born in Madrid, Spain, to Spanish singer [Julio Iglesias](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002960/?ls) and Spanish-Filipino socialite [Isabel Preysler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1923355/?ls). In 1979, his parents' marriage was annulled. He was eight years old when he moved to the U.S., and at the age of 15, secretly began writing music. He studied business administration at the University of Miami for a year before he dropped out to pursue a musical career. Five years later, on September 25, 1995, he released his first album at 18 years of age. His second album, which was recorded in Spanish, was released on January 29, 1997.  
  
Iglesias has made 10 albums. "Insomniac" was released 2008 and he did the official song for UEFA Europa League 2008, "Can You Hear Me", which he sang at the soccer league's finale. After "Insomniac" he made "Greatest Hits" and went on tour in 2009. His album "Euphoria" was his first bilingual album, featuring Spanish and English songs. His latest album "Sex and Love" was also bilingual.  
  
Iglesias has sold over 137 million records worldwide, making him one of the best selling Latin artists ever. He has more number-one songs on Billboard's charts, more than any other single male artist.  
  
Iglesias has recorded advertisements or provided songs for major brands, including Salsa Doritos (2002), PepsiCo (2003), Viceroy (2004), Tommy Hilfiger (2005), Azzaro (2009) Atlantico (2011-present), Soap opera theme songs (2013, 2014), Coty (2014), and Kia Soul (2014-2015). He also had guest acting roles on Once Upon a Time in Mexico, Two and a Half Men, and How I Met Your Mother.  
  
Iglesias has supported many charities, including City of Hope, Red Cross, Music for Relief, Habitat For Humanity, Help for Heroes, Live Earth, Muscular Dystrophy Association, Music for Relief, Special Olympics, The Salvation Army, Alex's Lemonade, and Hunger Relief.

Justin Drew Bieber was born on March 1, 1994 at St. Joseph's Hospital in London, Ontario, Canada and was raised in Stratford, Ontario. He is the son of [Pattie Mallette](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4399261/?ls) and [Jeremy Bieber](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4291153/?ls). He is of French-Canadian, Irish, German, English, and Scottish descent. He has three younger half-siblings via his father.  
  
Growing up, he showed a strong interest in music and taught himself to play many instruments, including, guitar, drums, piano and trumpet. His mother began posting videos of him performing musically on YouTube. The videos soon built up a fan following and caught the attention of talent agent [Scooter Braun](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4025993/?ls). Braun was able to secure an impromptu audition with [Usher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0713378/?ls), who was impressed and helped Bieber to sign a record deal.  
  
In 2009, his first single, "One Time", was a worldwide hit and was certified Platinum in Canada and the United States. This was followed by his debut EP album, "My World", which was also an international success. He became the first artist to have seven songs from a debut record chart on the Billboard Hot 100.  
  
In 2010, he released his first full-length studio album, My World 2.0. He also released a successful concert film, [Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1702443/?ls).  
  
In 2012, he released his third studio album, Believe. In 2015, he released his fourth studio album, Purpose.  
  
He has won a Grammy Award and an American Music Award. He has been listed numerous times by Forbes magazine among the "Top Ten Most Powerful Celebrities in the World."  
  
He has sold an estimated 140 million records, making him one of the world's best-selling music artists.

In 2005, Chávez joined a new telenovela Rebelde as Juan "Giovanni" Méndez López, a mischievous and rebellious student at a private boarding school in Mexico. Chávez became widely known for his ever-changing hair colors. The soap opera was transmitted in 65 other countries, including the United States, Mexico, Serbia, Peru, Romania, Brazil, Spain, Slovenia, Bulgaria Slovakia, Croatia and Albania. A major plot line of the show revolved around a group of six students forming a pop band. A notable aspect of the series is that Chávez and five of his other co-stars ( [Maite Perroni](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1671647/?ls), [Dulce María](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0555902/?ls), [Anahí](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0025584/?ls), [Alfonso Herrera](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1270781/?ls) and [Christopher Von Uckermann](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0879804/?ls)) became actual members of a real life band RBD. RBD created most of the music used on the show, and the six quickly became one of the most popular music acts in Latin America.  
  
As part of RBD, Chávez went on to receive two Latin Grammy nominations, achieving multi-platinum status with more than 22 million digital downloads and more than 17 million albums sold worldwide. He has performed concerts in 23 countries in 116 cities, 15,000 articles of merchandising, and selling more than 3,000,000 concert tickets and 4 million DVDs.  
  
RBD's first album Rebelde, was released on November 30, 2004 by EMI. The first three singles ("Rebelde" (lead single), "Sólo Quédate En Silencio" and "Sálvame") were all number one hits in Mexico, with the fourth single, "Un Poco De Tu Amor" reaching number two.  
  
RBD's first national tour, Tour Generación RBD, included 45 sold out dates in Mexico including three visits in Monterrey performing for more than 150,000 fans. The tour was certified by OCESA as the fourth most rapidly sold tour in Mexican history. In July 2005 a live CD/DVD, Tour Generación RBD En Vivo was released documenting their tour around Mexico (45 sold-out concerts across the country, including sixteen in Mexico City alone).  
  
In 2005 RBD released their second studio album, Nuestro Amor. This album set new record sales in Mexico, selling 127,000 copies on its release day, and 160,000 copies within its first week. In the U.S., the album topped the Latin Albums Chart for 3 weeks and peaked at #88 on the Billboard 200. The first four singles reached number one in Mexico. In the United States "Nuestro Amor", "Aún Hay Algo" and "Este Corazón" charted on the Hot Latin chart at #6, #24 and #10 respectively. Nuestro Amor also brought RBD a nomination for the Latin Grammy Awards in the category "Best Pop Album by a Group or Duo". They performed a new version of "Tras de Mí" at the ceremony.  
  
RBD's concert at the Los Angeles Coliseum is one of the fastest selling concert in the venue's history, beating megastar Madonna. In 2006, RBD sold 750,000 tickets becoming the 14th top selling act of 2006 worldwide.  
  
In November 2006, RBD released their third studio album Celestial produced and directed by Carlos Lara which debuted at number 15 in the Billboard 200, marking first-week sales of over 137,000 copies in the U.S. The album however did not have a full week of album sales, due to its Friday release. Despite this, it became their first album to peak or chart within the top 20 of the Billboard 200  
  
In December of 2006, RBD released their first English album Rebelswhich debuted at number 40 on the Billboard 200 album chart with first-week sales of 94,000 copies. Included on the album was "Tu Amor" a ballad written by Diane Warren and sung by Chavez.  
  
In 2007, RBD became spokespeople for Pepsi and appeared in numerous ads televised throughout Latin America. In 2008, RBD performed for over 500,000 fans in Brazil, breaking the record previously held by the Rolling Stones. On August 14, 2008, RBD announced through a press release that they would disband in 2009. To this day, RBD is considered the most successful pop group in Mexican history.  
  
In June 2007, Chávez appeared briefly in the stage show Hoy No Me Puedo Levantar, and in May 2008 he participated in Avenida Q (the Mexican version of Avenue Q), where he played the main puppet characters Eugenio (Princeton) and Rodri (Rod); his presence on the shows was intended to be one of the main box office attractions.  
  
After RBD's breakup, Chávez launched his career as a solo recording artist. His first studio album Almas Transparentes, peaked at number 56 on the Mexican pop charts.  
  
In 2011, Chávez turned heads with the provocative music video for his single "Libertad" featuring singer Anahi which became an instant sensation on YouTube with more than 1,000,000 views within three days of its upload. The video featured Chávez in a church confessional telling a priest he was not sorry for his sexual preference. The video featured a cameo by Perez Hilton. "The video looks super sexy," gushed Hilton on his blog PerezHilton.com. "It's inspired us to unleash our own libertad." "Libertad" continues to be an anthem for gay youth throughout Latin America. Esencial Released 2012  
  
On August 14, 2012, Chávez released the highly anticipated album Esencial, an acoustic compilation of songs performed at his show in São Paulo, Brazil in January 2012. People Magazine called the albums release "the return of Christian Chávez". A red carpet presentation of Esencial was held in Mexico City in June. Chavez performed duets with RBD co-star [Maite Perroni](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1671647/?ls) and Mexican Pop/Rock Singer [Ana Obregón](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0643505/?ls).  
  
"Sacrilegio", a track on Esencial also released as a single, immediately landed in the top 10 on Mexican pop charts. Other notable songs on the album include "No Me Olvides", written for Chávez by Mexican singer Juan Gabriel, and a remake of "¿En Donde Estas?" sung as a duet with Indonesian pop star Agnes Monica.  
  
In early March 2007, a magazine published pictures of Chávez signing documents and exchanging rings with another man, allegedly his Canadian boyfriend (and later identified as B.J. Murphy), outing Chávez with them. The pictures had been taken in 2005, the year in which gay marriages became legal in Canada. Chávez declared in March 2007, that the photos showed a part of him that he had not been willing to discuss previously.With his announcement, Chávez became the first openly gay Latin recording artist in history.  
  
On 30 March 2007, after Chávez's announcement of being gay, Ricky Martín told The Associated Press of his solidarity with Chávez's public declaration, saying, "Life is too short to live closed up, guarding what you say...(Chávez) has to be free in many aspects. I wish him much strength." Though Chavez is outspoken in supporting gay rights and opposing homophobia, he remains one of a handful of openly gay Latin actors and recording artists. He has been the face of numerous HIV awareness campaigns.  
  
In 2009, Chávez confirmed divorcing his husband. The reason for their separation has been the subject of much speculation, but Chávez insists that their relationship did not end on bad terms: "[Murphy] is a person I love and respect; I also admire him as a professional."  
  
In March 2012, Chávez confirmed dating Los Angeles Real Estate Agent Ben Kruger after photos of them together were published in the tabloid TV Notas. and later People en Español.  
  
In May 2012, People Magazine reported that Chavez had signed on as a spokesperson for the 2012 Reelection Campaign of [Barack Obama](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1682433/?ls).

Christian Chavez was born on August 7, 1983 in McAllen, Texas, U.S. At the age of two, he Moved to Mexico City.  
  
In 2002, Chávez was cast as Fernando 'Fercho' Lucena in the telenovela Clase 406. The series had four seasons and 350 one-hour episodes in total.  
  
In 2005, Chávez joined a new telenovela Rebelde as Juan "Giovanni" Méndez López, a mischievous and rebellious student at a private boarding school in Mexico. Chávez became widely known for his ever-changing hair colors. The soap opera was transmitted in 65 other countries, including the United States, Mexico, Serbia, Peru, Romania, Brazil, Spain, Slovenia, Bulgaria Slovakia, Croatia and Albania. A major plot line of the show revolved around a group of six students forming a pop band. A notable aspect of the series is that Chávez and five of his other co-stars ( [Maite Perroni](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1671647/?ls), [Dulce María](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0555902/?ls), [Anahí](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0025584/?ls), [Alfonso Herrera](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1270781/?ls) and [Christopher Von Uckermann](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0879804/?ls)) became actual members of a real life band RBD. RBD created most of the music used on the show, and the six quickly became one of the most popular music acts in Latin America.  
  
As part of RBD, Chávez went on to receive two Latin Grammy nominations, achieving multi-platinum status with more than 22 million digital downloads and more than 17 million albums sold worldwide. He has performed concerts in 23 countries in 116 cities, 15,000 articles of merchandising, and selling more than 3,000,000 concert tickets and 4 million DVDs.  
  
RBD's first album Rebelde, was released on November 30, 2004 by EMI. The first three singles ("Rebelde" (lead single), "Sólo Quédate En Silencio" and "Sálvame") were all number one hits in Mexico, with the fourth single, "Un Poco De Tu Amor" reaching number two.  
  
RBD's first national tour, Tour Generación RBD, included 45 sold out dates in Mexico including three visits in Monterrey performing for more than 150,000 fans. The tour was certified by OCESA as the fourth most rapidly sold tour in Mexican history. In July 2005 a live CD/DVD, Tour Generación RBD En Vivo was released documenting their tour around Mexico (45 sold-out concerts across the country, including sixteen in Mexico City alone).  
  
In 2005 RBD released their second studio album, Nuestro Amor. This album set new record sales in Mexico, selling 127,000 copies on its release day, and 160,000 copies within its first week. In the U.S., the album topped the Latin Albums Chart for 3 weeks and peaked at #88 on the Billboard 200. The first four singles reached number one in Mexico. In the United States "Nuestro Amor", "Aún Hay Algo" and "Este Corazón" charted on the Hot Latin chart at #6, #24 and #10 respectively. Nuestro Amor also brought RBD a nomination for the Latin Grammy Awards in the category "Best Pop Album by a Group or Duo". They performed a new version of "Tras de Mí" at the ceremony.  
  
RBD's concert at the Los Angeles Coliseum is one of the fastest selling concert in the venue's history, beating megastar Madonna. In 2006, RBD sold 750,000 tickets becoming the 14th top selling act of 2006 worldwide.  
  
In November 2006, RBD released their third studio album Celestial produced and directed by Carlos Lara which debuted at number 15 in the Billboard 200, marking first-week sales of over 137,000 copies in the U.S. The album however did not have a full week of album sales, due to its Friday release. Despite this, it became their first album to peak or chart within the top 20 of the Billboard 200  
  
In December of 2006, RBD released their first English album Rebelswhich debuted at number 40 on the Billboard 200 album chart with first-week sales of 94,000 copies. Included on the album was "Tu Amor" a ballad written by Diane Warren and sung by Chavez.  
  
In 2007, RBD became spokespeople for Pepsi and appeared in numerous ads televised throughout Latin America. In 2008, RBD performed for over 500,000 fans in Brazil, breaking the record previously held by the Rolling Stones. On August 14, 2008, RBD announced through a press release that they would disband in 2009. To this day, RBD is considered the most successful pop group in Mexican history.  
  
In June 2007, Chávez appeared briefly in the stage show Hoy No Me Puedo Levantar, and in May 2008 he participated in Avenida Q (the Mexican version of Avenue Q), where he played the main puppet characters Eugenio (Princeton) and Rodri (Rod); his presence on the shows was intended to be one of the main box office attractions.  
  
After RBD's breakup, Chávez launched his career as a solo recording artist. His first studio album Almas Transparentes, peaked at number 56 on the Mexican pop charts.  
  
In 2011, Chávez turned heads with the provocative music video for his single "Libertad" featuring singer Anahi which became an instant sensation on YouTube with more than 1,000,000 views within three days of its upload. The video featured Chávez in a church confessional telling a priest he was not sorry for his sexual preference. The video featured a cameo by Perez Hilton. "The video looks super sexy," gushed Hilton on his blog PerezHilton.com. "It's inspired us to unleash our own libertad." "Libertad" continues to be an anthem for gay youth throughout Latin America. Esencial Released 2012  
  
On August 14, 2012, Chávez released the highly anticipated album Esencial, an acoustic compilation of songs performed at his show in São Paulo, Brazil in January 2012. People Magazine called the albums release "the return of Christian Chávez". A red carpet presentation of Esencial was held in Mexico City in June. Chavez performed duets with RBD co-star [Maite Perroni](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1671647/?ls) and Mexican Pop/Rock Singer [Ana Obregón](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0643505/?ls).  
  
"Sacrilegio", a track on Esencial also released as a single, immediately landed in the top 10 on Mexican pop charts. Other notable songs on the album include "No Me Olvides", written for Chávez by Mexican singer Juan Gabriel, and a remake of "¿En Donde Estas?" sung as a duet with Indonesian pop star Agnes Monica.  
  
In early March 2007, a magazine published pictures of Chávez signing documents and exchanging rings with another man, allegedly his Canadian boyfriend (and later identified as B.J. Murphy), outing Chávez with them. The pictures had been taken in 2005, the year in which gay marriages became legal in Canada. Chávez declared in March 2007, that the photos showed a part of him that he had not been willing to discuss previously.With his announcement, Chávez became the first openly gay Latin recording artist in history.  
  
On 30 March 2007, after Chávez's announcement of being gay, Ricky Martín told The Associated Press of his solidarity with Chávez's public declaration, saying, "Life is too short to live closed up, guarding what you say...(Chávez) has to be free in many aspects. I wish him much strength." Though Chavez is outspoken in supporting gay rights and opposing homophobia, he remains one of a handful of openly gay Latin actors and recording artists. He has been the face of numerous HIV awareness campaigns.  
  
In 2009, Chávez confirmed divorcing his husband. The reason for their separation has been the subject of much speculation, but Chávez insists that their relationship did not end on bad terms: "[Murphy] is a person I love and respect; I also admire him as a professional."  
  
In March 2012, Chávez confirmed dating Los Angeles Real Estate Agent Ben Kruger after photos of them together were published in the tabloid TV Notas. and later People en Español.  
  
In May 2012, People Magazine reported that Chavez had signed on as a spokesperson for the 2012 Reelection Campaign of [Barack Obama](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1682433/?ls).

# 5 Musicians and Singers Born in November

[**Post**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/list/)[**Subscribe**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/subscribe/)

 Posted 2023-11-13 by [**Jennifer Muirhead**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/writer/644/) ⇒ [**follow**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/follow/644/)

Have you ever wondered whether you share a birthday with a famous musician or singer? Here are a few born during the month of November.   
  
**1. Tina Arena - November 1, 1967**  
  

[![Image 3](https://images.toopa.com/1182756_871855529693_l_Tina_Arena_Portrait.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182756_871855529693_Tina_Arena_Portrait.jpg)

_Tina Arena. Photo by John Diavola - Australian Council for the Arts._

  
  
 Lydia 'Tina' Arena is a singer-songwriter and musician from Melbourne, who first rose to fame by appearing on the TV show _Young Talent Time_ in the 70s and 80s. She has won seven ARIA awards. Her most recent album, _Love Saves_ was released in 2023.   
  
**2. Sophie B. Hawkins - November 1, 1964**  
  

[![Image 4](https://images.toopa.com/1182758_499199932914_l_Sophie_B_Hawkins.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182758_499199932914_Sophie_B_Hawkins.jpg)

_Sophie B. Hawkins._

  
  
 Tina Arena shares her birthday with the American singer-songwriter Sophie B. Hawkins. Her single _Damn I Wish I Was Your Lover_ , from her debut album _Tongues and Tails_, was a huge hit in 1992.   
  
**3. Sean 'Puffy' Combs - November 4, 1969)**  
  

[![Image 5](https://images.toopa.com/1182812_278345427404_l_Sean_Combs_2010.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182812_278345427404_Sean_Combs_2010.jpg)

_Image from Wikimedia Commons._

  
  
 American rapper and singer Sean Combs, aka. Puff Daddy, P. Diddy, or Diddy, was born in Harlem on November 4th, 1969. His debut album, _No Way Out_, was certified seven times platinum.   
  
  
**4. Tina Turner - November 26, 1929.**  
  

[![Image 6](https://images.toopa.com/1182804_780804439984_l_Tina_turner_21021985_01_350.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182804_780804439984_Tina_turner_21021985_01_350.jpg)

_Photo by Helge Øverås._

  
  
 Born Anna Mae Bullock, Tina Turner was born in Brownsville, Tennessee on November 26th, 1939). Her hits included _We Don't Need Another Hero_ (the theme song to the film _Mad Max 3: Beyond the Thunderdome_) and _Nutbush City Limits_, to which a line dance was taught in schools across Australian in the '80s.   
  
  
**5. Jimi Hendrix - November 27, 1942**  
  

[![Image 7](https://images.toopa.com/1182759_837574703756_l_Jimi_Hendrix_1967.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182759_837574703756_Jimi_Hendrix_1967.jpg)

_Photo by A. Vente, Wikimedia Commons._

  
  
 The legendary American guitarist, singer and songwriter, Jimi Hendrix, was born in Seattle on the 27th of November, 1942. He received many music awards, both during his lifetime and posthumously.

# 5 Musicians and Singers Born in November

[**Post**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/list/)[**Subscribe**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/subscribe/)

 Posted 2023-11-13 by [**Jennifer Muirhead**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/writer/644/) ⇒ [**follow**](https://www.weekendnotes.com/everywhere/follow/644/)

Have you ever wondered whether you share a birthday with a famous musician or singer? Here are a few born during the month of November.   
  
**1. Tina Arena - November 1, 1967**  
  

[![Image 3](https://images.toopa.com/1182756_871855529693_l_Tina_Arena_Portrait.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182756_871855529693_Tina_Arena_Portrait.jpg)

_Tina Arena. Photo by John Diavola - Australian Council for the Arts._

  
  
 Lydia 'Tina' Arena is a singer-songwriter and musician from Melbourne, who first rose to fame by appearing on the TV show _Young Talent Time_ in the 70s and 80s. She has won seven ARIA awards. Her most recent album, _Love Saves_ was released in 2023.   
  
**2. Sophie B. Hawkins - November 1, 1964**  
  

[![Image 4](https://images.toopa.com/1182758_499199932914_l_Sophie_B_Hawkins.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182758_499199932914_Sophie_B_Hawkins.jpg)

_Sophie B. Hawkins._

  
  
 Tina Arena shares her birthday with the American singer-songwriter Sophie B. Hawkins. Her single _Damn I Wish I Was Your Lover_ , from her debut album _Tongues and Tails_, was a huge hit in 1992.   
  
**3. Sean 'Puffy' Combs - November 4, 1969)**  
  

[![Image 5](https://images.toopa.com/1182812_278345427404_l_Sean_Combs_2010.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182812_278345427404_Sean_Combs_2010.jpg)

_Image from Wikimedia Commons._

  
  
 American rapper and singer Sean Combs, aka. Puff Daddy, P. Diddy, or Diddy, was born in Harlem on November 4th, 1969. His debut album, _No Way Out_, was certified seven times platinum.   
  
  
**4. Tina Turner - November 26, 1929.**  
  

[![Image 6](https://images.toopa.com/1182804_780804439984_l_Tina_turner_21021985_01_350.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182804_780804439984_Tina_turner_21021985_01_350.jpg)

_Photo by Helge Øverås._

  
  
 Born Anna Mae Bullock, Tina Turner was born in Brownsville, Tennessee on November 26th, 1939). Her hits included _We Don't Need Another Hero_ (the theme song to the film _Mad Max 3: Beyond the Thunderdome_) and _Nutbush City Limits_, to which a line dance was taught in schools across Australian in the '80s.   
  
  
**5. Jimi Hendrix - November 27, 1942**  
  

[![Image 7](https://images.toopa.com/1182759_837574703756_l_Jimi_Hendrix_1967.jpg)](https://images.toopa.com/1182759_837574703756_Jimi_Hendrix_1967.jpg)

_Photo by A. Vente, Wikimedia Commons._

  
  
 The legendary American guitarist, singer and songwriter, Jimi Hendrix, was born in Seattle on the 27th of November, 1942. He received many music awards, both during his lifetime and posthumously.

## Biography

*   #### Born

26 November 1998 (age 27)

*   #### Born In

Île-de-France, France

1) Simon Rosenfeld (born 26 November 1998) is a French singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and record producer from Paris.

Rosenfeld has been building momentum since his first single, “Do It For Me,” came out in 2018 and was streamed in the tens of millions. Born and raised in Paris, Rosenfeld’s music resonates with romance and intimacy, drawing inspiration both from his classical background and from the renowned French electronic music scene. Following the success of his debut EP, The Red Room, in the US, Rosenfeld signed with APG in 2021, exploring more modern sounds and a more raw and almost scandalous songwriting style.

In 2023, Rosenfeld decided to reconnect with his hometown and signed with Warner Music France, gearing up for his debut album, Blood & Porcelain. This project explores Rosenfeld’s personal and artistic identity crisis. It was followed in 2024 by a short film directed by Rosenfeld, split into three music videos.

2) Thrash metal act from Tokyo, Japan, formed in November 1986. Rosenfeld features vocalist/frontman Hisayoshi Hiraga as the only permanent member. In 1986 the band started out with Yasuhiro Kamei (gt), Hajime Morii (b) & Takafumi Segawa (ds). In December 1987 Kamei left the band and Rosenfeld's activities were put on hold. As a result Hisayoshi joined [ＡＩＯＮ](https://www.last.fm/music/%EF%BC%A1%EF%BC%A9%EF%BC%AF%EF%BC%AE) in January 1988, playing his first gig with the band on March 13th. In June 1989 he leaves the band to restart Rosenfeld, and he does so with Youichi Horizoe on guitar as a replacement for Kamei. They released two albums: _"Pigs of the Empire"_ in 1991 and live album _"In the Garden"_ in 1994. They also made four demo tapes across their career _"Rosenfeld"_, _"B"_, _"Ashes to Ashes"_ and _"demo '93"_.

A few member changes follow in the early 90's:  
July 1990: Gish ([Rapes](https://www.last.fm/music/Rapes)) replaces Morii on bass & Kouichi ([Rapes](https://www.last.fm/music/Rapes)) replaces Segawa on drums  
January 1991: Hiromi joins on guitar to become a five piece, twin guitar, band  
March 1992: Hiromi and Gish leave the band after 'The God's Truth' compilation is released (3.16)  
October 1992: Takami ([Bellzlleb](https://www.last.fm/music/Bellzlleb), Salamander) replaces Gish on bass and Shinji ([Guilty Vice](https://www.last.fm/music/Guilty+Vice), Snaggle Tooth) replaces Hiromi on guitar

The band split-up in March 1993 due to personal difficulties. In the meantime Hisayoshi starts his new project called [Skull Crusher](https://www.last.fm/music/Skull+Crusher). Rosenfeld regroups for the last time in October with Takashi Kinoshita replacing Takami on Bass and Hirofumi Ozawa replacing Kouichi on Drums so they can hold their last gigs with the final being on December 23rd 1993. But then, in 2008, the band reunited.

Among several other Japanese thrash metal bands like [Rommel](https://www.last.fm/music/Rommel) and [Harkenkreuz](https://www.last.fm/music/Harkenkreuz), Rosenfeld had a Nazi-image. They wrote lyrics about Nazism and POW's. Rosenfeld used the imagery for shock value.

## Biography

*   #### Born

26 November 1998 (age 27)

*   #### Born In

Île-de-France, France

1) Simon Rosenfeld (born 26 November 1998) is a French singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and record producer from Paris.

Rosenfeld has been building momentum since his first single, “Do It For Me,” came out in 2018 and was streamed in the tens of millions. Born and raised in Paris, Rosenfeld’s music resonates with romance and intimacy, drawing inspiration both from his classical background and from the renowned French electronic music scene. Following the success of his debut EP, The Red Room, in the US, Rosenfeld signed with APG in 2021, exploring more modern sounds and a more raw and almost scandalous songwriting style.

In 2023, Rosenfeld decided to reconnect with his hometown and signed with Warner Music France, gearing up for his debut album, Blood & Porcelain. This project explores Rosenfeld’s personal and artistic identity crisis. It was followed in 2024 by a short film directed by Rosenfeld, split into three music videos.

2) Thrash metal act from Tokyo, Japan, formed in November 1986. Rosenfeld features vocalist/frontman Hisayoshi Hiraga as the only permanent member. In 1986 the band started out with Yasuhiro Kamei (gt), Hajime Morii (b) & Takafumi Segawa (ds). In December 1987 Kamei left the band and Rosenfeld's activities were put on hold. As a result Hisayoshi joined [ＡＩＯＮ](https://www.last.fm/music/%EF%BC%A1%EF%BC%A9%EF%BC%AF%EF%BC%AE) in January 1988, playing his first gig with the band on March 13th. In June 1989 he leaves the band to restart Rosenfeld, and he does so with Youichi Horizoe on guitar as a replacement for Kamei. They released two albums: _"Pigs of the Empire"_ in 1991 and live album _"In the Garden"_ in 1994. They also made four demo tapes across their career _"Rosenfeld"_, _"B"_, _"Ashes to Ashes"_ and _"demo '93"_.

A few member changes follow in the early 90's:  
July 1990: Gish ([Rapes](https://www.last.fm/music/Rapes)) replaces Morii on bass & Kouichi ([Rapes](https://www.last.fm/music/Rapes)) replaces Segawa on drums  
January 1991: Hiromi joins on guitar to become a five piece, twin guitar, band  
March 1992: Hiromi and Gish leave the band after 'The God's Truth' compilation is released (3.16)  
October 1992: Takami ([Bellzlleb](https://www.last.fm/music/Bellzlleb), Salamander) replaces Gish on bass and Shinji ([Guilty Vice](https://www.last.fm/music/Guilty+Vice), Snaggle Tooth) replaces Hiromi on guitar

The band split-up in March 1993 due to personal difficulties. In the meantime Hisayoshi starts his new project called [Skull Crusher](https://www.last.fm/music/Skull+Crusher). Rosenfeld regroups for the last time in October with Takashi Kinoshita replacing Takami on Bass and Hirofumi Ozawa replacing Kouichi on Drums so they can hold their last gigs with the final being on December 23rd 1993. But then, in 2008, the band reunited.

Among several other Japanese thrash metal bands like [Rommel](https://www.last.fm/music/Rommel) and [Harkenkreuz](https://www.last.fm/music/Harkenkreuz), Rosenfeld had a Nazi-image. They wrote lyrics about Nazism and POW's. Rosenfeld used the imagery for shock value.
